LA TIMES: Ex-U.S. ambassador says Mexico's former president feared Sinaloa boss would expose corrupt officials

June 22, 2026 | 🔴

📰 The LA Times amplifies Ken Salazar's memoir claim that AMLO feared "El Mayo" would "spill the beans" on corrupt officials — sourced entirely to an anonymous businessman Salazar calls "the Whisperer."

💀 Lower in the same piece: Salazar told the paper he "never saw any proof" tying AMLO to the cartels.

• "I never saw any proof of it" — Salazar, on AMLO–cartel ties
• Claim came from "the AMLO whisperer, someone who was a friend and confidant"

NYT: Mexican Officials Have Become Informants for the Trump Administration
June 27, 2026 | 🔴

📰 The NYT headline recasts cross-border law-enforcement cooperation as Mexican officials turning "informants for the Trump administration" — the word frames Mexico's institutions as assets run from Washington, not a sovereign partner.

🇲🇽 Sheinbaum has said for months that US agents do not run operations on Mexican soil; the headline quietly asserts the reverse without showing its work.

Source

🇲🇽📊 INFLATION DOWN TO 3.55% — AND BANXICO NAMES WASHINGTON AS THE DRAG

Mexico's inflation fell to 3.55% in early June, down from 4.45% in April and the lowest since October, and Banxico held its rate at 6.50%. The one risk the central bank flagged for investment through 2026 wasn't domestic policy — it was "uncertainty over the trade relationship with the United States" and the looming T-MEC review. The drag on Mexico's economy has a return address.

🇲🇽🚆 MEXICO IS BUILDING PASSENGER RAIL AGAIN — BY THE STATE, FOR THE PUBLIC

The first AIFA–Pachuca train rolls July 25; the Mexico City–Querétaro and Mexico City–Pachuca lines open in 2027. The price tag: 750 billion pesos, with 33,072 military engineers laying track — 6,380 of them women. The passenger rail that neoliberal privatization killed in the 1990s is back on public tracks.

🇲🇽🇻🇪 WHILE WASHINGTON SQUEEZES CARACAS, MEXICO SENDS PLANES

After the twin earthquakes that struck Venezuela on June 24, Sheinbaum deployed 250 rescue personnel and Air Force flights loaded with humanitarian aid. Of 73 Mexican nationals the embassy reached, 26 asked to come home — all reported safe and in good health. South–South solidarity, no strings attached.

🇲🇽🌎 COOPERATION WITH WASHINGTON ON SECURITY — YES. SUBORDINATION — NEVER.

Sheinbaum says coordination with the US has cut fentanyl trafficking and tightened the border, but drew the line where it matters: "no foreign agent interference in national territory is permitted." Washington's ambassador handed Sonora 26 patrol trucks and 8 all-terrain vehicles. Mexico takes the help — on its own terms, not orders.

🚨🇲🇽 IN MEXICO, WELFARE IS NO LONGER A FAVOR TRADED FOR VOTES

"Social programs no longer depend on the vote." Sheinbaum said it handing Mujeres Bienestar pensions to women aged 60–64 in Tuxtla Chico, Chiapas — marking the break from the neoliberal era when welfare was a favor doled out at the ballot box. Under the 4T, pensions and scholarships are written into the Constitution. Rights, not handouts.

🇲🇽🏭 MEXICAN EXPORTS JUMP 25.4% IN MAY — TRADE SURPLUS HOLDS THROUGH THE TARIFF WAR

INEGI reported Mexican exports hit $69.5 billion in May, up 25.4% year-on-year — non-oil exports up 25.6%, manufactured goods up 25.1% to nearly $63 billion. The trade balance stayed in surplus at $2.26 billion, and the five-month surplus reached $5.77 billion — versus just $918 million in the same period last year.

🚨🇲🇽 MEXICO REQUESTED 269 EXTRADITIONS FROM THE US SINCE 2018 — IT HAS RECEIVED ZERO

Between January 2018 and May 2026, Mexico filed 269 extradition requests with the United States — for organized crime, ex-governors' corruption, the Ayotzinapa case. Washington has returned exactly none. "¿Cuántos han sido devueltos a México? Ninguno," Sheinbaum said — 36 requests rejected, 233 still pending, among them ex-Tamaulipas governor Cabeza de Vaca.

🏳️‍⚧️🇲🇽 SHEINBAUM ON TRANS RIGHTS: STATE GOVERNMENTS MUST DO THEIR PART

As trans activists enter an eighth day of protest outside the Interior Ministry, Sheinbaum backed their demands and pointed to where much of the work lives: "Los registros civiles dependen de los estados" — civil registries, gender-identity recognition and birth-certificate changes are state matters. Their demands include specialized medical care, hormone therapy and a National Trans Law; housing, she said, should come through universal programs like Vivienda para el Bienestar, not segregated schemes.
